description: AegisSat develops the Space Mission Architecture Simulator for Space Mission Design Game. Backed by TRL-7 flight heritage (KÜPSAT-01, 25.64km apogee, TPMK 2025/007159) & IAC 2026 study (IAC-26-C2.IPB.29, AA7075-T6/CFRP/Rigid 10K), we pair radiation shielding with WERR 24-Byte 0-SRAM FNS avionics & Negative Schwarzian/Koenigs ADCS. Stress-test CubeSats against NASA SPENVIS/OMNIWeb solar storms & SEU bit-flips. Live: https://aegissat.space | Code: https://github.com/bdagli-web/aegissat
summary:
AegisSat is an interactive 3D Space Mission Design Game and CubeSat engineering simulator for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (https://aegissat.space/ with 7-slide PDF presentation at https://aegissat.space/docs/AegisSat_Presentation_EN.pdf). Players design 1U CubeSat missions across NASA's four segments—Launch, Space, Ground, and User Science Return—navigating three progressive tiers (Cadet Stratospheric Probe, Flight Engineer Artemis Lunar, Principal Investigator Mars Deep Space) plus Sandbox and 4-Player Co-Op NASA Mission Design Lab (MDL) mode with live JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and 8 engineering gates. Dual Three.js 3D viewports provide real-time 1U Hardware Twin and NASA Mission Viz orbital trajectory visualization.

Every trade-off is anchored in verified aerospace research: KÜPSAT-01 TRL-7 stratospheric flight heritage (25.64 km apogee, 22.51 hPa, -54.50 °C ambient, +37.23 °C passive thermal delta, 421 samples), our IAC 2026 Antalya composite shield (IAC-26-C2.IPB.29, 345 g Al7075-T6 / Toray T700 CFRP, 81.7% Von Mises stress reduction, FS 27.20), and WERR 24-Byte (192-bit) Zero-SRAM avionics (0.0 SEU flips/day, 192/192 CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE single-bit detection, 94.37% 10-cycle Negative Schwarzian and Koenigs ADCS damping at mu = 0.75, Patent 2 Julia Watchdog TR 2026/016633, and Patent 3 Collatz Parity Spoofing Barrier TR 2026/020266). Live space weather integrates NOAA SWPC, NASA DONKI, and Microsoft Planetary Computer data.
details: CHALLENGE ALIGNMENT & INTERACTIVE USER EXPERIENCE AegisSat transforms NASA's four mission design segments—Launch, Space, Ground, and User Science Return—into an interactive Three.js 3D spacecraft and NASA Mission Viz trajectory simulation game. Players engineer 1U CubeSats across three progressive tiers: Level 1 Cadet Stratospheric Probe, Level 2 Flight Engineer Artemis Lunar Transfer, and Level 3 Principal Investigator Mars Deep Space with Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and Solar Particle Events (SEP). A Free Sandbox mode lets users experiment with custom subsystems, while In-Flight Random Events (Martian dust storms, coronal mass ejections, and ground-station blackouts) test mission resilience. The simulation dynamically tracks 8 engineering gates and JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4): GEVS 14.1 Grms launch vibration compatibility, 1,330 g 1U mass limit, Solar EPS power balance (accounting for 45% solar irradiance at Mars), UHF/S-Band/Ka downlink capacity, mission budget, -30 °C internal thermal survival floor, radiation bit-flip immunity, and User Science Return scoring. Collaborative NASA Mission Design Lab (MDL) 4-player co-op mode allows specialized roles—Mission Commander, Structures & Thermal Lead, Avionics & Cyber-ADCS Engineer, and Science & Payload Lead—to sign off on flight gates. Interactive features include shareable #design= URL states, an interactive CubeSat 101 handbook, a global mission leaderboard, an instant English/Turkish bilingual switcher, and a responsive zero-overflow interface across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. VERIFIED HARDWARE FLIGHT HERITAGE, COMPOSITE SHIELDING & ZERO-SRAM AVIONICS Every constraint in AegisSat is grounded in verified flight data, peer-reviewed aerospace studies, and patented avionics architectures: • KÜPSAT-01 Stratospheric Flight Heritage (TRL-7, Launched 7 August 2026, Mersin, TPMK 2025/007159): Achieved 25,636 m true apogee, 22.51 hPa pressure, and -54.50 °C ambient temperature (-17.27 °C internal, demonstrating +37.23 °C passive thermal retention). Survived ~20 G burst shock and peak rotational tumble of 3,647.58 deg/s. All 421 flight telemetry samples are verified and replayed inside the simulator. • Structural & Thermal Composite Shielding (IAC 2026 Antalya, IAC-26-C2.IPB.29): 345 g 1U hybrid chassis utilizing AA7075-T6 aerospace aluminum, Toray T700 carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP), ceramic-infused Rigid 10K resin, and extruded polystyrene (XPS). Achieved an 81.7% Von Mises stress reduction (from 100.87 MPa down to 18.49 MPa), a primary resonant frequency of 100.76 Hz under NASA GEVS 14.1 Grms qualification, and a structural factor of safety (FS) of 27.20. With a total bus mass of 373 g, AegisSat delivers 957 g of usable payload margin within the 1,330 g 1U limit. Dual-stage thermal protection holds -24.5 °C internal temperature in -150.0 °C deep space via passive MLI (+37.23 °C retention) combined with a thermostatic 0.50 W survival heater, maintaining a lean 0.85 W deep-space bus. • WERR 24-Byte Zero-SRAM Deterministic Avionics & Cyber-ADCS (Patent TR 2026/020266 & TR 2026/016633): Eliminates mutable neural weight SRAM entirely (0 Bytes mutable weight SRAM vs 64 MB ARM SRAM subject to 234.0 single-event upsets per day). Employs 72-Byte Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) PROM, achieving 192/192 single-bit SEU detection via CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE framing. Non-linear ADCS detumbling combines Negative Schwarzian derivative control and Koenigs eigenfunction damping (mu = 0.75, S(f)(0) = -6.9196 < 0), delivering 94.37% 10-cycle kinetic energy damping compared to 63.15% for tuned PID and 29.97% for SEU-degraded ARM architectures. Enhanced with a Julia Repeller AI Watchdog and 2-adic Haar/Collatz spoofing barrier (gamma_crit = 0.58496) to prevent command injection. Validated through 9/9 automated bit-exact Python and JavaScript unit and parity tests passing in continuous integration. NASA & PARTNER OPEN DATA INTEGRATION (/api/space-weather) AegisSat dynamically streams real space environment data through Cloudflare Pages Edge Functions (/api/space-weather): • NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Notification, Knowledge, Information): Real-time Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) events, Coronal Mass Ejections (CME), and geomagnetic solar storm warnings. • NASA OMNIWeb & SPENVIS: Solar wind speed, interplanetary magnetic field (IMF), and trapped radiation belt proton/electron flux profiles for LEO, Lunar, and Mars orbital envelopes. • NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC): Real-time GOES >=10 MeV energetic proton flux, planetary Kp-index, and X-ray flux tracking solar radiation storms. • Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API: High-resolution multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2 L2A) covering the KÜPSAT-01 Mersin Mediterranean launch and recovery corridor. • NASA Science Mission Directorate (SMD) & GSFC Mission Design Lab (MDL): Mission life cycle guidelines, concurrent engineering review gates, and JPL CML 1–4 validation criteria. • NASA CSLI CubeSat 101 Handbook & JPL Mission Viz: Subsystem standards, GEVS launch environments, and 3D trajectory visualization reference frameworks. • Meteomatics Weather API: Real-time surface wind speed, barometric pressure, and atmospheric launch window safety envelopes. PROJECT DELIVERABLES & REPOSITORIES • Live Mission Simulator & Game: https://aegissat.space/ • 7-Slide English Presentation PDF: https://aegissat.space/docs/AegisSat_Presentation_EN.pdf • 7-Slide Turkish Presentation PDF: https://aegissat.space/docs/AegisSat_Presentation_TR.pdf • Interactive Web Presentation (English): https://aegissat.space/demo/slides_en.html • Interactive Web Presentation (Turkish): https://aegissat.space/demo/slides_tr.html • Open-Source GitHub Repository & Test Suite: https://github.com/bdagli-web/aegissat • KÜPSAT-01 TRL-7 Flight Report: https://teknosanat.com.tr/lib/cubesat/cubesat_master_flight_report_tr.html SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE In full alignment with NASA Space Apps Challenge Super Intelligence guidelines, generative AI tools assisted with boilerplate user-interface scaffolding and generating the original AegisSat mission patch artwork (Mission Patch SI-Assisted). The mission patch is entirely original and contains zero NASA logos, flags, official emblems, or copyrighted marks. All flight mechanics, orbital equations, GEVS vibration formulas, 24-byte CRC-16 framing algorithms, Negative Schwarzian ADCS control laws, flight telemetry logs, and Python-to-JavaScript parity tests were independently developed, validated, and verified by our engineering team with 9/9 automated unit tests passing in continuous integration.
